chapter_theme: Impure Saivism (அசுத்த சைவம்): Saivas of service and rite, known by outward signs such as earrings, seals and rudraksha beads and by recitation; the chapter then turns to those who see further, the severe pure Saiva and the jnani.
structure_note: 1423 and 1424 describe the Saiva of outward signs; 1425 and 1426 move beyond them to the severe pure Saiva and the jnani, which sits oddly under this heading.

1423.reading: For those on the paths of service and rite it is fitting to praise the paired holy feet and, without lapse, to wear the signs: paired earrings, the two seals and the paired rudraksha garland at the neck.
1423.nuance: சரியை and கிரியை are the first two of the four Saiva paths (with yoga and jnana): temple service and ritual worship. The signs are outward, which is why this is called impure Saivism, meaning mixed with form rather than wrong. தினையார், ஈரணை முத்திரை and இணைக்கண்ட மாலை are taken by tradition as earrings, seals and a rudraksha garland; the exact objects are uncertain.

1424.reading: One who wears two gold earrings, keeps the two inner bonds on the body, tests himself, follows the twelvefold way and keeps reciting is one kind of Saiva.
1424.nuance: துவாதச மார்க்கம் (the twelvefold way) may be the breath's reach of twelve finger-breadths beyond the head, or a twelve-syllable mantra; the verse doesn't say. உட்கட்டு இரண்டு (two inner bindings) is obscure. ஒருசைவர், 'one kind of Saiva', places such a person within Saivism without praise.

1425.reading: Those who have seen the nine divisions have seen the rare thing, and those who see the divisions are the severely pure Saivas.
1425.nuance: கண்டம் is a division or region (the nine regions of the earth) and also the throat, and the verse puns on it and கண்ட (saw) in every line. What the nine divisions are, in the world or in the body, can't be fixed from the verse. It names the severe pure Saiva of chapter 90, not the impure one.

1426.reading: The jnani is one who comes to see all the good books of the earth, the way of silence, all sixty-four attainments, the other planes, the end of the unwritten Veda, and himself together with the Lord.
1426.nuance: எழுதா மறை, the unwritten scripture, is the Veda kept by mouth, and its end (ஈறு) Vedanta. எண்ணெண் is sixty-four. The list climbs from books to silence to seeing oneself with the Lord (கோனொடு தன்னையும்), which is the last and highest item.

links.note: 1423 commends earrings, seals and beads for those of service and rite; 1438 says the pure Saiva goes beyond outward garb (வேடம் கடந்து), without show. The signs are fitting at one stage and passed beyond at another.

1423 assigns the paired earrings, seals and rudraksha garland to those of chariyai and kiriyai (அணைவாஞ் சரியை கிரியையினார்க்கே). 1670 says the emblems are not futile (அவமான சாதனம் ஆகாது) for Siva-gnanis and Siva-yogis and, on its plain reading, futile for the others (அவமாம் அவர்க்கு). The conflict holds on that plain reading of 1670, which gives the signs to the higher paths where 1423 gives them to the lower; on the other reading of அவமாம் அவர்க்கு the two agree.

1424 describes a Saiva who wears two gold earrings (காதுப்பொன் ஆர்ந்த கடுக்கன்) and keeps reciting (ஓதி இருப்பார்), and calls him only 'one kind of Saiva'. 1662 lists ash, copper earrings (காதணி தாம்பிர குண்டலம்) and the rudraksha string as Rudra's emblems for those who recite (ஓதியவர்க்கும்). The same earrings-and-recitation figure is placed by 1424 at the lower, outward grade of Saivism and by 1662 among the marks of the Siva-yogi.

1425 says those who have seen the nine divisions (கண்டங்கள் ஒன்பதும் கண்டவர்) have seen the rare thing. 2221 is a first-person report: knowing the intent, the speaker saw the nine regions fit together (ஒன்பது கண்டமும் ஆங்கே பொருந்தறிந்தேன்) and then knew the Lord of the gods in his fullness. Both make the seeing of the nine கண்டம் the step to knowing the Lord, and 2221's sequence helps read the obscure punning of 1425.

1426 lists what the jnani sees: all the good books of the earth (நன்னூல் அனைத்து), the way of silence, the sixty-four attainments, and finally himself with the Lord (கோனொடு தன்னையும்). 1461 says letters, songs and the sixty-four arts (எண்ணெண் கலை) do not remove fettered birth (பாசப் பிறவியும் நீங்கா). Read together, the books and arts in 1426's list are not themselves release; what counts is the last item, seeing oneself with the Lord.

source_issues: 1425 names கடுஞ்சுத்த சைவர் and 1426 the ஞானி, though the chapter heading is impure Saivism; the verses may be misplaced or the headings arranged later.
